relevance_note: GHB biomarker study in dried bloodspots of confirmed SSADHD patients; Table 1 gives per-patient age and GHB for 'all nineteen patients characterized' post-newborn, and the text individually describes a sibship ('female, 2^nd newborn screen (GHB=111 μM) and again at 8.7 years').
method_note: Rows built with a short Python script from my own reading; every value was checked by hand against Table 1 and the text, and every span verified verbatim by script. Table 1 has three column groups side by side (Post-Newborn Bloodspots: Age (yrs), GHB (μM); Newborn Bloodspots: Age (hrs), GHB (μM); Control Post-Newborn Bloodspots). Labels 'Table 1 row k' refer to the k-th data row of the Post-Newborn column group (k counted below the sub-header row 'Age (yrs) | GHB (μM)'); the text says these 19 DBS are 19 distinct patients ('all nineteen patients characterized'). Age values from that table are the age at DBS collection (column 'Age (yrs)'), recorded as age at last evaluation, as printed without the unit; ISO values use decimal years. The sibship described in Results was matched to Post-Newborn rows by age and GHB (male: 6.8 y, 187 μM = row 7; female: 8.7 y, 160 μM = row 10); the text does not give the row. Newborn column group: 12 DBS from nine patients; rows are samples, not people, and except for the sibship the paper does not say which samples belong to which patient or whether those patients are also among the 19 post-newborn patients. So no individual rows were created for the other newborn-only patients (at most 7 people), to avoid inventing or duplicating persons; their GHB values are not attributed. The control column row with footnote d (age 3, GHB 545) is the previously reported patient [10] with combined SSADH deficiency and Rett syndrome, labelled 'ref [10] patient' (rule 4) rather than a table-row label, to avoid a clash with the Post-Newborn row labels; her sex and 'developmentally delayed' come from the title of reference [10] as printed in the reference list ('...deficiency in a developmentally delayed female'). The four unaffected controls are out of scope. Group-level only (not attributed): 11M/8F sex split and 4 sibships among post-newborn patients; newborn DBS origin (California, Texas, Maryland, Ireland). No ALDH5A1 variant is printed for any person and molecular analysis is described only as part of 'a combination' for the group, so the variants table is empty. No total patient count is stated (nine newborn-DBS patients and nineteen post-newborn patients, overlap not given), so n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null. No clinical features are reported per patient; all checklist items are 'not reported'. No contradictions found; no stacked cells.
